business-api-context

Business API map

What the API of the system under test (tuDeclaracion.com) means to the business: how callers are admitted, the journeys that cross several calls, the architecture behind them and the integrations at the edge. Built from code and migrations; there is no OpenAPI spec.

Overview

tuDeclaracion has almost no API of its own. An accountant signs in, picks a client company, uploads the month's accounting TXT and downloads the PADI file for the tax authority. Nearly all of that work is done by the browser talking straight to Supabase (Postgres through its REST layer, five stored functions and Supabase Auth) under the accountant's own session. The Next.js server adds only a session gate, two auth landing routes, four small Server Actions and the pages that read data for review.

So the business rule "an accountant sees only their own clients" is not written in an endpoint. It lives in database Row Level Security policies, and every browser call depends on them. The exchange-rate lookup is the one place where the server holds a privilege the user does not: it alone writes the shared BCU rate cache. Auth emails (sign-up confirmation, password recovery) leave through a signed webhook that a Supabase Edge Function turns into a Resend message.

Part of the surfaceWhat it lets the business doFound in
Supabase Auth, called from the browserSign up, log in with email or Google, request and finish a password recovery.src/app/signup/page.tsx, src/app/login/login-client.tsx, src/app/forgot-password/page.tsx
2 route handlersTurn an emailed link or a Google return into a session and send the user on.src/app/auth/confirm/route.ts, src/app/auth/callback/route.ts

Size of the surface, counted from code: 2 route handlers, 4 Server Actions, 5 RPCs, 1 Edge Function, 1 middleware and 3 tables the browser updates directly (cuenta, declaracion, declaracion_1376). The repository has no OpenAPI spec and no REST controllers, so this map was built from code and migrations only (user-approved substitute; see discovery-gaps).

Permission and auth model

One scheme is in use: a Supabase Auth session, kept by the browser in sb-* cookies (Secure in production, SameSite Lax, not HttpOnly by design). It is obtained by email and password, by Google (OAuth code exchange) or by an emailed one-time link. There are no API keys, no bearer tokens issued by the app and no roles: the only human actor is the accountant. The tiers below are therefore about where a request is stopped, not about who the caller is.

Reading the flow

  • 1. Sign-up or recovery calls Supabase Auth straight from the browser, with a Turnstile token when the site key is set.
  • 2. Auth hands the email to the send-email function through a signed hook; the function renders Spanish copy and sends it with Resend.
  • 3. The link points at /auth/confirm?token_hash=...&type=.... The route handler runs verifyOtp and redirects to next, which safeInternalPath restricts to same-origin paths.
  • 4. Google returns to /auth/callback, which exchanges the OAuth code for a session and fills cuenta.nombre from the Google profile when empty.
  • 5. From then on middleware revalidates the session on each page request, and the browser sends the same session to Supabase on every direct data call.

Where enforcement rests only on RLS

Anything the browser does through supabase-js never passes through Next.js code, so no application check exists in front of it. The tables the browser changes directly are listed below; the policies come from the migrations, not from the live database.

TableBrowser operationsPolicies found in migrationsNote
cuentaUPDATE name (Mi cuenta; Google name fill in the callback)select own, update ownNo insert or delete policy; the row is created by the sign-up trigger.
declaracionUPDATE estado on first PADI download; insert and delete through RPCsselect, insert, update, delete via empresa.cuenta_idThe browser chooses the status value; only the check constraint limits it.
declaracion_1376UPDATE estado on download; INSERT by the review page on first open (server, user session)select, insert, update, delete via empresa.cuenta_idA GET of the review page writes a row.
empresa, plan_cuentas, mapeo_1376, asientoReads direct; writes only through the 5 RPCsempresa: all four; plan_cuentas and mapeo_1376: select, insert, delete; asiento: select, insert, delete (no update)The RPCs are security invoker: a caller who passes another account's p_empresa_id is stopped only by these policies.

The Next.js-side guards are small: haySesion() in the two rate Server Actions, and getUser plus redirect in each server-rendered page. seleccionarEmpresaActiva has no session or ownership check; it only stores a cookie that is re-validated by RLS when read (see discovery-gaps).

Journey: sign up and verify the email

An accountant opens an account; nothing in the product works until the emailed link has been used. Figure in auth-model (steps 1 to 7).

  • 1. The sign-up form calls supabase.auth.signUp with the trimmed email and password, the Turnstile token (when the site key is set) and the chosen plan as metadata. Why: there is no server endpoint for registration; Supabase Auth is the endpoint.
  • 2. Supabase creates the auth.users row and a trigger mirrors it into cuenta. Why: users have no insert policy on cuenta.
  • 3. Auth calls the Send Email hook. The function verifies the signature, builds the link and sends it with Resend. Why: Supabase's own mailer is test-only and rate-limited.
  • 4. The page shows "Revisa tu correo" whatever the delivery outcome after a successful signUp. A duplicate email shows its own error.
  • 5. The user opens the link: GET /auth/confirm?token_hash&type runs verifyOtp and redirects to next (default /inicio). On failure the user lands on /login?error=verification-failed.

Endpoints involved: supabase.auth.signUp (Supabase Auth, wire path is Supabase's, not read from this repo); hook POST to Edge Function send-email; GET /auth/confirm.

Entities touched: cuenta (see entities and flow-account-access in business-data-context)

Feature and journey ids: journey-signup-verify, FEAT-001 in business-e2e-context

Journey: log in (password or Google)

A returning accountant reaches the product through one of two doors that end in the same session cookie.

  • 1. Password: signInWithPassword with the Turnstile token; on success the page pushes /inicio. The UI shows a fixed Spanish message chosen by the stable error code, never the raw message.
  • 2. Google: signInWithOAuth with redirectTo = {APP_URL}/auth/callback. Google and Supabase handle the consent; the browser comes back with a code.
  • 3. GET /auth/callback exchanges the code for a session, fills cuenta.nombre from the Google profile only when empty, and redirects to next (same-origin only). A denial or failed exchange goes to /login?error=google-auth-failed.
  • 4. Middleware sends an anonymous visitor of a gated page to /login?redirect={path}, and sends a signed-in visitor of /login, /signup or /forgot-password to /inicio.

Endpoints involved: supabase.auth.signInWithPassword, supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth; GET /auth/callback; PostgREST PATCH cuenta (name fill).

Entities touched: cuenta (flow-account-access in business-data-context)

Feature and journey ids: journey-login, FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 in business-e2e-context

Journey: recover a password

An accountant who lost the password regains access. This is a security path: it turns an email address into a session.

  • 1. The form calls resetPasswordForEmail with redirectTo = /auth/confirm?type=recovery&next=/reset-password and the Turnstile token. Every error except captcha_failed is swallowed on purpose, so the page never reveals whether the email has an account.
  • 2. Auth calls the Send Email hook; the function sends the recovery message with a /auth/confirm link carrying token_hash, type=recovery and redirect_to (URL-encoded).
  • 3. The route handler reads token_hash, type and next; it does not read redirect_to. By code the user is redirected to the default /inicio, not to /reset-password. A bad link goes to /forgot-password?error=expired.
  • 4. On the reset page getUser must find the recovery session, then updateUser({ password }) sets the new password.

Endpoints involved: supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail, supabase.auth.updateUser; GET /auth/confirm; Edge Function send-email.

Entities touched: cuenta (identity only)

Feature and journey ids: journey-password-recovery, FEAT-004 in business-e2e-context; the redirect suspicion is the same one recorded in business-data-context discovery-gaps

Journey: create a company and make it active

The accountant adds a client company with its chart of accounts; without it nothing can be imported or declared.

  • 1. The browser validates name, RUT and plan rows, then calls rpc crear_empresa_con_plan_cuentas. Why: company and chart must be created in one transaction or not at all.
  • 2. The function runs as the caller (security invoker), so the insert policies of empresa and plan_cuentas decide, and a payload above the array cap is rejected before any write.
  • 3. Editing a company calls rpc editar_empresa_con_plan_cuentas, which replaces the whole plan.
  • 4. On /empresas "Ingresar al dashboard" calls the Server Action seleccionarEmpresaActiva(empresaId), which sets the HttpOnly cookie empresa_activa_id (30 days). Pages resolve the company from it and fall back to the newest company when it does not match one of the account.

Endpoints involved: RPC crear_empresa_con_plan_cuentas, RPC editar_empresa_con_plan_cuentas, Server Action seleccionarEmpresaActiva; PostgREST reads of empresa.

Entities touched: empresa, entity-plan-cuentas, flow-create-company in business-data-context

Feature and journey ids: journey-create-company, journey-select-company, FEAT-009 to FEAT-011 in business-e2e-context

Journey: import a month of accounting lines

The core act of the product: a month of lines becomes the data every PADI file is computed from. It is destructive when replacing.

  • 1. The browser parses the TXT, so a malformed file never reaches the server. All-or-nothing: any bad line rejects the file.
  • 2. If any USD line has rate 0, the browser calls poblarCotizacionesBcuParaPeriodo(periodo). The server (BCU has no CORS for browsers) asks BCU for the period range and writes the rates to the shared cache with the admin client. A failure stops the import with "No se pudo obtener la cotización".
  • 3. The browser reads the rate for each USD line from the cache (previous business day), then calls rpc insertar_asientos with the lines and a replace flag.
  • 4. The function rejects more than 20,000 lines (demasiadas_lineas), refuses an already processed period unless replace is set (periodo_ya_procesado), deletes the old lines when replacing, resets the 2181 status to abierta and inserts the lines. One transaction.

The amounts, the rate and the Libro and Tipo values arrive as caller-supplied JSON. Check constraints on asiento cover day, debe, haber, concepto, RUT and Tipo; they do not recompute totals or rates, so the parser in the browser is the only rule for them.

Endpoints involved: Server Action poblarCotizacionesBcuParaPeriodo; PostgREST GET cotizacion_bcu_cache; RPC insertar_asientos; BCU SOAP call (outbound).

Entities touched: entity-asiento, entity-declaracion, entity-cotizacion-bcu-cache, flow-import-period, flow-usd-rate in business-data-context

Feature and journey ids: journey-import-period, FEAT-014, FEAT-018 and FEAT-019 in business-e2e-context

Journey: review a period and download the PADI file

The accountant checks the computed result and downloads the regulatory text file. The file itself is never stored or sent by the API.

  • 1. The review page is rendered on the server with the user's session: it reads the period's lines, the plan and the mapping through the Supabase client and computes the result in memory. No application endpoint returns a "declaration".
  • 2. For the 1376 the first view of a period that has lines inserts the declaracion_1376 row on the server (a GET that writes). A period with no row for the 2181 redirects to /dashboard.
  • 3. The browser builds the file text and downloads it; nothing is sent to the server for the file.
  • 4. On the first download the browser calls PostgREST PATCH declaracion (2181) or declaracion_1376 with estado = generada. If that update fails the file is already downloaded and the page says so.

Endpoints involved: PostgREST GET asiento, plan_cuentas, mapeo_1376, codigo_linea_1376; PATCH declaracion; PATCH declaracion_1376; POST declaracion_1376 (server, user session).

Entities touched: entity-declaracion, state-declaracion, state-declaracion-1376, flow-generate-2181, flow-generate-1376 in business-data-context

Feature and journey ids: journey-review-2181, journey-review-1376, journey-configure-1376, FEAT-015 and FEAT-016 in business-e2e-context

Journey: delete a period

The only user-facing deletion. No undo; recovery means importing the TXT again.

  • 1. The dashboard dialog confirms and calls rpc borrar_periodo(p_empresa_id, p_periodo).
  • 2. The function deletes the 1376 row and the 2181 row of that company and period; the lines go by cascade. It has no ownership check of its own: it is security invoker, so the delete policies on both tables decide.
  • 3. The company, its plan and its mapping stay.

Endpoints involved: RPC borrar_periodo.

Entities touched: entity-declaracion, entity-asiento, flow-delete-period in business-data-context

Feature and journey ids: journey-delete-period, FEAT-017 in business-e2e-context

Architecture behind the API

It is one Next.js application (App Router, Bun runtime on Render for staging) on top of one Supabase project. There is no API gateway, no separate service and no queue. Three kinds of Supabase client exist: browser, server (cookie session) and admin (secret key, server only).

ComponentRolePersistence or integrations touchedWhy it matters for QA
Browser (client components)Parses the TXT, builds PADI text, calls Supabase directly.Supabase Auth, PostgREST, 5 RPCsMost business calls bypass Next.js, so API-level tests must hit Supabase, not the app URL.
middleware.tsRefreshes the session and gates 4 route prefixes on every request.Supabase Auth (getUser)A Supabase outage here affects every page, gated or not.
Next.js server (pages, actions, route handlers)Server-rendered review pages, 4 Server Actions, /auth/confirm, /auth/callback.Postgres (user session), BCU, admin client for the rate cacheSmall logic surface, but the auth landing routes decide who gets a session.
Supabase AuthIdentities, sessions, OTP links, Google, captcha verification.Send Email hook, Google, TurnstileHosted settings (hook, captcha, password length, Site URL) are outside the repo.
Postgres with RLS and 5 RPCsAll business data and tenant isolation.Tables, triggers, functionsTenant isolation lives only here; test it with two accounts.
send-email Edge FunctionVerifies the hook signature and sends the email.ResendSandbox sender: only the Resend account owner receives mail (see integrations).

What breaks if a part hangs: Auth down means no login and no page (middleware); BCU down means imports with USD lines fail and the rates screens degrade; the Edge Function down means new sign-ups and recoveries do not receive their link, while the UI still says "check your email" (see integrations).

Not at the boundary: PADI and DGI (the file is imported by hand outside the app) and Render (hosting). Nothing in the repo exposes an inbound webhook besides the Send Email hook.

Cross-references

Entities exposed directly to the browser

Every table below can be read through the browser client under RLS; the first three can also be updated directly. Entity detail lives in business-data-context: entities (cuenta, empresa), entity-plan-cuentas, entity-mapeo-1376, entity-asiento, entity-declaracion, entity-cotizacion-bcu-cache.

  • Direct update: cuenta, declaracion, declaracion_1376.
  • Direct read, RPC write: empresa, plan_cuentas, mapeo_1376, asiento.
  • Direct read only: codigo_iva, codigo_linea_1376, cotizacion_bcu_cache (server writes).
  • Orphans: three tables in the generated types (declarations, data_fields, declaration_required_fields) have no migration and no caller; whether the live database exposes them is unknown (already recorded in the data map).

Features this API backs

Journeys: journey-signup-verify, journey-login, journey-password-recovery, journey-create-company, journey-select-company, journey-import-period, journey-review-2181, journey-review-1376, journey-configure-1376, journey-delete-period in business-e2e-context (features feature-auth, feature-account, feature-company, feature-declarations, feature-rates).

API-only paths not caught as features

  • Direct calls to the 5 RPCs and to PostgREST with the user's own session: a user can call them outside the UI. Only the column checks and RLS apply, not the browser parser rules.
  • The Send Email hook and the two Server Actions that call BCU have no screen of their own; they are reached through sign-up, recovery and import.
  • Auth callbacks /auth/confirm and /auth/callback appear in the journeys but not as features.

Where the rest lives

There is no OpenAPI file and bun run api:sync was not run: api/openapi-types.ts in this QA repository is the boilerplate stub. For columns and function signatures the contract is the migrations in ../tudeclaracion/supabase/migrations/ and the generated types in ../tudeclaracion/src/types/supabase.ts.

Discovery gaps

Not verified

  • No OpenAPI spec exists and capability api-schema was not available, so the map was built from code (user-approved). Consequence: staleness is detected only through repo-path sources, never through an openapi: source.
  • RLS policies, grants and RPC definitions were read from the migrations, not from the live database. Whether every migration is applied on staging, and whether anon can read anything, is unconfirmed.
  • Nothing was executed against staging: no call, no login, no request was made. Every step above is cited to a file, none confirmed by a run.
  • Supabase wire paths (/auth/v1/..., /rest/v1/...) are not in this repository; endpoints are named by the supabase-js method or table, not by HTTP path.
  • Hosted Supabase settings: whether the Send Email hook is on, SEND_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET is set, captcha is enforced server side, Google is configured, email confirmation is required, minimum password length and Site URL. supabase/config.toml holds local values only.
  • Environment variable NAMES were read from ../tudeclaracion/.env.example (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_*, SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, RESEND_API_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL). BCU needs none. SEND_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET is read by the function but absent from .env.example.
  • Production: host, URL and settings unknown, so none of the above is confirmed for it.
  • Rate limits: Supabase Auth limits, and any limit on RPCs or the two BCU Server Actions, are not visible in the repo.
  • Whether the generated types' extra tables (declarations, data_fields, declaration_required_fields) answer PostgREST on the live project.
  • Legacy input: .context/business/business-api-map.md does not exist in this QA repository, so nothing was migrated.
  • Journey cap: 10 journeys exist in business-e2e-context; 7 are traced here. journey-select-company (a cookie action), journey-configure-1376 (one more RPC, guardar_mapeo_1376) and journey-review-1376 are folded into the create-company and review sections rather than traced separately.
  • Monorepo shards: none (single repository). The supabase/functions/ folder holds only send-email.

Suspected defects and risks (verified in code, not reproduced)

New findings of this pass. The ones already in the data and e2e maps (login ignores ?redirect, recovery lands on /inicio, silent ?error= banners, plan limits not enforced) are not repeated.

  • /auth/confirm consumes the one-time token on a plain GET. An email scanner or link previewer that opens the link first can use it up, and the user then sees "verification-failed" or "expired". Applies to sign-up and recovery.
  • Forgot-password treats every error except a captcha failure as success. A hook or Resend failure therefore shows the same "check your email" confirmation as a sent message (by design for privacy, but it hides delivery failures).
  • seleccionarEmpresaActiva checks neither session nor ownership and stores any string. A cookie with a foreign or unknown id falls back silently to the newest company, so a user can work on a different company from the one they picked with no notice. Isolation still holds through RLS.
  • poblarCotizacionesBcuParaPeriodo(periodo) and reintentarCotizacionBcu are callable by any signed-in user and trigger BCU calls and shared-cache writes. periodo is not validated against the YYYYMM format and there is no throttle or timeout, so repeated calls can load BCU and the cache table.
  • insertar_asientos takes amounts, rate, Libro and the status reset from the caller. A direct RPC call can store inconsistent values for the caller's own company, and the file is later computed from them; the browser parser is the only guard for those fields.
  • The browser sets estado = generada itself. Any signed-in user can set that status on their own period without having downloaded the file.
  • The review page for the 1376 creates a row on GET. Anything that fetches the URL (prefetch, a refresh) changes data; low impact, but it breaks the GET-is-safe expectation.

Cross-check against the data and e2e maps

Coherent: every journey above maps to an e2e journey and to data flows of the same name, and every integration in the e2e integrations section appears here. Entities without an API surface: codigo_linea_1376 has read access only. No journey touches an entity absent from the data map.
